name: Comparative Empirical Study of Code-Generation Prompting Strategies
executive_summary: An empirical benchmark comparing multiple prompting strategies head-to-head specifically on code-generation tasks, rather than proposing a new technique.
description: Systematically benchmarks several prompting strategies (varying levels of decomposition, exemplar use, and reasoning structure) against each other on code-generation benchmarks, providing empirical guidance on which strategies actually help for this domain rather than assuming general-purpose reasoning techniques transfer directly.
when_to_use: Choosing among competing code-generation prompting strategies for a specific deployment and wanting empirical, not just theoretical, guidance.
known_pitfalls: Benchmark results are specific to the models and code-generation benchmarks tested; may not transfer to a materially different model or task distribution.

primary_source.title: A Comparative Empirical Study of Prompting Strategies for Code Generation

usage_templates.template: For task {{coding_task}}, generate solutions using each strategy in {{strategy_list}}, run each against the test suite {{test_suite}}, and report pass rate per strategy.

variables.name: strategy_list
variables.description: The set of prompting strategies being compared

variables.name: test_suite
variables.description: The executable test suite used to score correctness

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.

corpus_file: A Comparative Empirical Study of Prompting Strategies for Code Generation.pdf
